label: Skyrim humanoid (99-bone)
socketRotationNotes: Quaternion XYZW taking weapon-asset space into ANY socket bone's local space on this rig. Weapon GLBs preserve their native NIF node axes (Skyrim authors a weapon along its attach node's +Z), while the imported armature stores bones in Blender's convention (bone +Y along the node's +Z for a Z-axis game). That is a fixed -90 degrees about X between the two frames, so it belongs to the rig, not to any one weapon: every weapon and every socket on this rig needs exactly this rotation and nothing else. Verified against the built GLB - the corrected blade axis tracks the hand's pinky-to-index grip axis to within 12 degrees across SWORD_IDLE, GUARD and LIGHT_1, and hangs the sheathed sword down and back off the left hip.
notes: Bone names are the niftools-renamed HKX names; sockets confirmed against the built GLB. Beast races share this rig: Skyrim ships no beast body skeleton, only the five auxiliary tail bones declared below.

tail.notes: Skyrim has no beast body skeleton: Khajiit and Argonians animate on this same 99-bone rig, and skeletonbeast.nif differs from skeleton.nif only by these five tail bones. Tails are driven by a parallel auxbone clip set whose files share their names with the body clips, so a tail animation is matched automatically. The tail skeleton's own coordinates are relative to its attach bone's head, which is how the chain lands in character space with no hand-measured offset.

socketNotes: Named bones the game has to find by name. Most are attachment points; `head` is not — it is there so a first-person view can collapse the head the camera sits inside, without the game having to know which meshes are a face on which race.
